 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the appellant/petitioner challenging the judgment and award dated 08.05.2017 passed in MVC No.11/2011 by the Senior Civil Judge & MACT, Sedam (for short, 'the Tribunal') seeking enhancement of compensation.
NC: 2024:KHC-K:3828-DB 2.
Parties are referred to as per their ranking before the Tribunal.
Appellant is the petitioner and the respondents are the respondents before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts leading to rise filing of this appeal are as under:
That, on 26.01.2009, the petitioner was proceeding to Bangalore in NEKRTC Bus bearing Reg.KA-32/F-1370. The respondent No.1 was the driver of the said Bus.
In the early morning on NH No.7 near PVC Pipes Factory, the driver of the said bus drove the bus in a rash and negligent manner, in a high speed and lost control over the bus and dashed to a Lorry.

Due to the accident, the petitioner sustained grievous Bhimreddy S/O Sharanareddy Patil vs Basawaraj And Ors on 13 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/76615419/
2 injuries and he was admitted to initially GGH Ananthpur Hospital and later he was shifted to Padman Chandra Super Specialty Hospital at Karnool.

sentences.text: The petitioner spent huge amount towards his medical treatment.

It is stated that, the petitioner was an agriculturist and earning Rs.50 lakh per annum and due to accident, he lost his income and claiming compensation NC: 2024:KHC-K:3828-DB filed claim petition under Section 166 of M.V. Act before the Tribunal for the injuries sustained by him in the road traffic accident.
4. The petitioner got dismissed the petition against respondent No.1.
The respondent No.2 though appeared did not chose to file written statement.
The respondent No.3 appeared through counsel and filed written statement denying the entire averments made in the claim petition and prayed to dismiss the claim petition.
5. The Tribunal, on the basis of the pleadings of the parties framed relevant issues.
The petitioner, in order to prove his case examined himself as PW.1 and in order to prove the disability, examined the doctor as PW.2 and produced 33 documents at Exs.P1 to P-33.
Respondents have not stepped into witness box nor produced any documents.

The Tribunal, after recording the evidence, hearing on both sides and on the assessment of oral and documentary evidence, answered issue No.1 in the affirmative, answered issue Nos.2 and 4 partly affirmative NC: 2024:KHC-K:3828-DB and issue No.5 as per final order.
The claim petition was partly allowed and the Tribunal ordered that the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.4,65,134/- with 6% interest.
It is held that the respondent Nos.2 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to compensation and directed them to deposit the compensation amount within a period of 60 days from the date of order.

The petitioner,
aggrieved by the judgment filed this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation.

6. Heard the learned counsel for the petitioner and also learned counsel for respondent Nos.2 and 3.
7.
Learned counsel for the appellant/petitioner submits that, the petitioner has suffered permanent disability and he is unable to do his day-to-day work.

He also submits that pursuant to the order passed by this Court, the petitioner/appellant has appeared before the Medical Board and the Medical Board after examining the petitioner has submitted a report to this Court after assessing the disability at 58%.
Hence, he submits that NC: 2024:KHC-K:3828-DB the Tribunal has committed an error in assessing the disability at 20% which is on the lower side.
He also submits that the compensation awarded under other heads is on the lower side.
Hence, prayed to allow the appeal by enhancing the compensation.

8. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent Nos.2 and 3 supports the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal and submits that the Tribunal was justified in assessing the disability at 20% to the whole body and compensation granted under other heads are just and proper.
On these grounds, he prays to dismiss the appeal.
9. Perused the records and considered the submissions of the learned counsel for the parties.
The point that arises for our consideration is quantum.

sentences.text: It is not in dispute that, the petitioner met with an accident on 26.01.2009 when he was proceeding in a NEKRTC Bus the driver of which due to his negligence NC: 2024:KHC-K:3828-DB driving dashed the Lorry and sustained grievous injuries.

In order to prove that the accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of the offending Bus, the petitioner has produced certified copies of FIR and charge sheet, which are marked at Exs.P1 and P3.
11.

Insofar as quantum of compensation, the learned counsel for the petitioner contended that prior to the accident, the petitioner was hale and healthy, aged about 30 years and was doing agriculture and was earning Rs.50 lakh per annum from the agricultural source.
But due to the accident, he has suffered permanent disability and lost the income deriving from his agricultural land.
In order to establish that, he is an agriculturist produced copy of Lavani Patrika which are marked as Exs.P.24 and 25 and also produced RTCs which are marked as Exs.P.26 to 29.
Perusal of the same establishes that the petitioner is an agriculturist, however to show the income as claimed by the petitioner, no documents are produced before the Court.

In the absence of proof of income and taking note NC:
2024:KHC-K:3828-DB of the avocation of the petitioner, we are the of the view that assessment of monthly income of the petitioner at Rs.7,500/- would be appropriate given in the peculiar facts and circumstances of the case.
12. Further, in order to prove the disability, the petitioner examined the doctor as P.W.2, who examined the petitioner and issued disability certificate marked as Ex.P.31.
The doctor has opined that the petitioner has suffered disability of 60% to the whole body.
However, the Tribunal has assessed the disability at 20% to the whole body, which is on the lower side.

This Court vide order dated 17.07.2023 directed the petitioner to appear before the Medical Board on 26.07.2023 at 11.00 a.m. and the Medical Board was called upon to examine the petitioner and file its report.
Pursuant to the order dated 17.07.2023, the Medical Board has submitted a report and opined that the petitioner has suffered a permanent disability at 58%.

In view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Jithendran Vs. The NC: 2024:KHC-K:3828-DB New India Assurance Company Limited and another reported in (2022) 15 SCC 620, wherein the Apex Court held that "the Courts should be mindful of the fact that even though the physical disability is assessed at 69%,
the functional disability is 100% in so far as claimant's loss of earning capacity is concerned."

entities.text: Jithendran Vs. The NC: 2024:KHC-K:3828-DB New India Assurance Company Limited and another reported in (2022) 15 SCC 620
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
By applying the law laid down by the Apex Court in the case of Jithendran (supra), we assess the functional disability of the petitioner at 100%.
13.

Insofar as the petitioner's loss of future earning capacity, the petitioner is also entitled for addition of 40% towards future income in view of the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Erudhaya Priya Vs. State Express Transport Corporation Ltd. reported 2020 SCC Online SC 601.

sentences.text: The petitioner is aged about 30 years at the time of the accident and multiplier applicable to his age group is '17' which is rightly taken by the Tribunal.

Considering the monthly income of the petitioner at Rs.7,500/- and the other factors as stated - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:3828-DB supra, the petitioner is entitled for compensation of Rs.21,42,000/-
(Rs.7,500/- + 40% =Rs.10,500 x 12 x 17 x 100%) on account of 'loss of future income'.

sentences.text:
Considering the evidence of PW-2, disability certificate and medical report submitted by the Medical Board, as ordered by this Court, we assess the compensation as under:
 Sl. Heads By this Court  No.
 1. Loss of future income Rs.21,42,000/-
 2. Towards medical  expenses Rs.2,72,734/-
 (maintained as it is  awarded by the  Tribunal)
 3. Pain and suffering Rs.1,00,000/-
 4. Towards attendant's Rs.60,000/-
 charges, food and  conveyance

5 . Towards loss of Rs.50,000/-
 amenities  6. Towards loss of income RS.45,000/-
 during the period of  treatment
Thus, the petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.26,69,734/- as against Rs.4,65,134/-, awarded by the Tribunal.

Hence, the petitioner is entitled for an enhanced compensation of Rs.22,04,600/- with interest @ 6% p.a.
16.

In view of the above discussion, we proceed to pass the following:
ORDER (a) The appeal is allowed in part.

(b) The impugned judgment and award dated 08.05.2017 passed by the Tribunal is modified.
(c) The petitioner is entitled for a total compensation of Rs.26,69,734/- as against Rs.4,65,134/-
awarded by the Tribunal.

The petitioner is entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.22,04,600/-
